program: Spin-off A v2: the pair-residual noise spectrometer with a scale-aware stochastic gate
lesson_from_v1: Run 1 (registrations 379ccbf2 and 03bd40d9, jobs dbfp6h8m94ac738u2pvg and dbfuqg0iudkc73e3bieg) returned NOT CONFIRMED on BOTH devices by the same gate: G3 required a VE drop >= 0.02 under injected depolarizing, and measured +0.0179 (marrakesh) and -0.0050 (fez). Diagnosis, verified mechanically and mathematically: VE is scale-invariant, and depolarizing compresses the D-matrix and the baseline residual proportionally, so on a device with non-negligible intrinsic residual the VE ratio does not move. The compression itself is large and parameter-free predicted: K = Var(D_arm)/Var(D_B) has exact theory values C1 1.427, C2 1.150, I 0.255, and run 1 measured C1 1.426/1.362, C2 1.135/1.089, I 0.251/0.280 (fez/marrakesh). v1 gates G0-G2 passed on both devices. This v2 replaces only the stochastic instrument; the physics claim is unchanged.
claim_under_test: Same spectrometer claim as v1, scored with the corrected instrument: blind to inversion-covariant miscalibration (ledger intact, potentials track the shifted parameter-free prediction), responsive to fresh coherent mismatch (VE drop, no compression), and responsive to genuine stochastic noise through D-variance compression matching the exact prediction K_I = 0.255.
experiment: Identical circuits, arms, shots, and conventions to v1: four arms, ONE job, ibm_fez, layout [141,142,143], seed_transpiler 42, 20k shot-equivalents/input, 36 pubs, ~480k shots (~130 QPU-seconds). Runner hardware/run_witness_fez.py unmodified. Fresh data only: the two v1 datasets are in-sample for these gates (both pass retrodictively) and cannot count as confirmation.
analysis_script: hardware/analyze_witness_v2.py, frozen at registration (gates embedded there must match)
coherent_gate_change: The v1 coherent gate (VE drop >= 0.05) shares VE's ratio blindness and passed marrakesh by only 0.011, so v2 gates the coherent arm on the drift-immune weighted mean-square-residual ratio R_C2 = MSresid(C2)/MSresid(B) >= 2 (v1 measured 3.34 marrakesh, 3.15 fez). The VE drop is reported but not gated.
in_sample_disclosure: Gate thresholds were calibrated on the v1 hardware runs and exact theory. Margins at calibration: K_I theory 0.255, measured 0.251 and 0.280 vs gate window [0.155, 0.355] and ceiling 0.5; K_C2 measured 1.135 and 1.089 vs floor 0.8; R_C2 measured 3.15 and 3.34 vs floor 2. Both v1 datasets pass all v2 gates retrodictively, which is precisely why they cannot count: only the fresh run decides.

decision_criteria.not_confirmed: any gate missed - report prominently, no reinterpretation; v1's two NOT CONFIRMED verdicts remain reported in full either way

pre_submission_health_check: Submit only if, at submission time, IBM's published calibration for the pinned layout satisfies: readout assignment error <= 0.03 on each of qubits 141/142/143 AND CZ error <= 0.01 on pairs (141,142) and (142,143). Values at registration (2026-10-27): readout 0.0127/0.0083/0.0049, CZ 0.0018/0.0021 -- thresholds are ~2.4x headroom over the worst current value, in the same calibration regime that produced v1 fez's VE_B = 0.943. If the check fails, do not submit; re-check on later calibration cycles. This rule is part of the registration and is decided before any v2 data exist.
output_data_file: data/witness_counts_v2_fez.json (the runner's scratch output is moved there so the v1 fez dataset is never overwritten)
budget_note: ~130 QPU-seconds (calibrated: v1 fez job measured 129 s). Open-plan window after both v1 runs leaves ample headroom.
timestamp_note: To be pushed to the PUBLIC repository (github.com/andrewmatlock/postselected-work-statistics) BEFORE submission, as with both v1 registrations.
no_post_hoc_changes: Any deviation from this plan is exploratory and must be labelled so.
